headline: Myths About Federal Criminal Cases You Should Ignore

publisher.name: Law Office of Angelo J. Reyes, APC

articleBody:
It's easy to get caught up in misinformation when facing federal charges. Let's clear up some common myths so you can make informed decisions.

Myth: Federal charges are always more serious than state charges.
Fact: While many federal crimes carry significant penalties, seriousness depends on the specific offense, not just the jurisdiction. Both state and federal cases can have life-altering consequences.

Myth: You can talk your way out of trouble with federal agents.
Fact: Anything you say can and will be used against you. It's always best to politely decline to answer questions and immediately ask for legal counsel. Don't try to explain or justify anything without your lawyer present.

Myth: Public defenders are less effective in federal court.
Fact: Federal public defenders are often highly experienced and knowledgeable. However, they may have heavy caseloads. A private attorney like Angelo Reyes can offer more individualized attention, which is crucial in complex federal cases.

Myth: If you're innocent, you don't need a lawyer.
Fact: Even innocent people need strong legal representation. The federal justice system is complex, and without an attorney who knows the ins and outs, you could inadvertently harm your own defense. Don't risk it.
